input.title: What motivates insurers to use derivatives: Evidence from the United Kingdom life insurance industry
input.abstract: Using firm-specific variables that proxy for the motivations of life insurers decision to participate in derivative transactions, we examine existing theories of corporate hedging behaviour. Our findings support the evidence of previous research that risk management and scale factors explain the use of derivatives. We observe a substitution effect that insurers use on-balance-sheet hedging through structuring their assets and liabilities to reduce price risks. © 2011 The International Association for the Study of Insurance Economics.
input.source: Geneva Papers on Risk and Insurance: Issues and Practice
